```typescript
import type { ChapterSpec } from "./chapters";

type Breakdown = { id?: string; field: string; fields?: string[]; title: string; columns: string[] };

/** One table per distinct grouping, in the chapter's authored priority order. */
export function distinctBreakdowns<T extends Breakdown>(groups: T[]) {
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  return groups.filter(group => {
    const key = (group.fields ?? [group.field]).join("+");
    if (seen.has(key)) return false;
    seen.add(key);
    return true;
  });
}

export function curatedBreakdowns<T extends Breakdown>(groups: T[], limit = 2) {
  return distinctBreakdowns(groups).slice(0, limit);
}

/** Configured source breakdowns that can actually be built from the loaded fields. */
export const explorerBreakdowns = (spec: Pick<ChapterSpec, "groups">, available: string[]) => distinctBreakdowns(spec.groups)
  .map(group => ({ id: group.id ?? group.field, title: group.title, fields: [...new Set([group.field, ...(group.fields ?? [])])].filter(field => available.includes(field)), metrics: group.columns }))
  .filter(group => group.fields.length);
```

SQL output aliases: well, what, independent, a, of, indicative

```typescript
import { definition } from "./definitions";
import { currentSnapshotMetrics, metricNotes } from "../semantics/evidence";

/**
 * Measures the model is most likely to conflate. Each entry names a lookalike
 * and the reason it is a different population or calculation, so the contract
 * says what a metric is NOT as well as what it is.
 */
const NOT_THE_SAME_AS: Record<string, [string, string][]> = {
  revenue: [["gross_revenue", "session revenue is earned, attributed to attended sessions; gross revenue is cash collected on sales"]],
  gross_revenue: [["revenue", "cash collected by payment date, not revenue earned by attendance"], ["net_revenue", "gross includes recorded GST"]],
  net_revenue: [["gross_revenue", "net is payment value less recorded GST"]],
  payroll_revenue: [["revenue", "monthly instructor attribution from Payroll, rounded; not Sessions"]],
  fill_rate: [["booking_fill_rate", "fill counts attendance, booking fill counts reservations"], ["show_up_rate", "show-up divides by booked seats, not capacity"]],
  booking_fill_rate: [["fill_rate", "bookings include no-shows and late cancels"]],
  show_up_rate: [["fill_rate", "denominator is booked seats, not capacity"]],
  avg_class_size_incl: [["avg_class_size_excl", "this one counts empty sessions"]],
  avg_class_size_excl: [["avg_class_size_incl", "this one excludes empty sessions"]],
  lost_revenue: [["revenue", "a what-if at current yield, never lost sales or a forecast"]],
  retention_rate: [["second_visit_rate", "in the current source these are the same number read from two columns; never present them as independent findings"]],
  second_visit_rate: [["retention_rate", "same number from a different column; not independent evidence"]],
  conversion_rate: [["lead_conversion_rate", "this is newcomer-trial conversion; the other is lead-stage conversion on a different population"]],
  lead_conversion_rate: [["conversion_rate", "lead cohort by creation date, not newcomer trials"]],
  active_base: [["active_memberships", "members versus memberships; both current snapshots with no history"]],
  active_memberships: [["active_base", "memberships versus distinct members"]],
  no_show_rate: [["late_cancel_rate", "no-shows exclude late cancellations; both divide by booked seats"]],
  late_cancel_rate: [["no_show_rate", "a late cancel is not a no-show"]],
  lapsed_members: [["churn_rate", "lapsed counts members by expiry period; do not assume the two agree"]],
  meta_leads: [["leads", "Meta-reported conversions are not CRM people; never add them to CRM leads"]],
  meta_roas: [["gross_revenue", "Meta-attributed purchase value, not CRM cash"]],
};

/** What population a measure describes, so a monthly cohort is never read as a snapshot or the reverse. */
function basis(id: string, domain: string, aggregation: string) {
  if (currentSnapshotMetrics.has(id)) return "current snapshot as of the source date; no historical or period comparison exists";
  if (id.startsWith("meta_")) return "Meta account reporting, network context; not studio-attributed and not CRM people";
  if (aggregation === "last") return "latest recorded state";
  if (domain === "revenue" && id.startsWith("gross")) return "cash collected, by payment date";
  return "selected period";
}

const AGGREGATION: Record<string, string> = {
  sum: "additive across rows and groups",
  weighted: "ratio: recompute numerator ÷ denominator; never average, add or compare it with a mean of group rates",
  avg: "average of records; not additive and sensitive to small samples",
  median: "median of records; not additive",
  last: "latest value; not additive over time",
};

/**
 * One governed line per metric, built from the registry rather than hand-copied,
 * so every one of the registered measures arrives with its formula, direction
 * and aggregation rule. Direction is the part models most often guess wrong:
 * a rising no-show rate is adverse, a rising fill rate is not.
 */
export function metricContract(id: string): string {
  const def = definition(id);
  if (!def) return `${id}: unavailable.`;
  const note = metricNotes[id];
  const formula = String(def.description ?? "").replace(/\s+/g, " ");
  const lookalikes = (NOT_THE_SAME_AS[id] ?? []).filter(([other]) => definition(other));
  return [
    `${id} (${def.label}): ${note?.definition ?? `Governed calculation ${formula.length > 220 ? formula.slice(0, 217) + "…" : formula}.`}`,
    note?.definition ? `Calculation: ${formula.length > 220 ? formula.slice(0, 217) + "…" : formula}.` : "",
    `Format ${def.format}. Basis: ${basis(id, def.domain, def.aggregation)}. Aggregation: ${AGGREGATION[def.aggregation] ?? def.aggregation}.`,
    `Direction: ${def.higherIsBetter ? "a rise is favourable" : "a rise is ADVERSE (lower is better)"}. Needs at least ${def.minSample} contributing records for a reliable reading.`,
    note?.caveat ? `Caveat: ${note.caveat}` : "",
    lookalikes.length ? "Not the same as: " + lookalikes.map(([other, why]) => `${other} (${definition(other)?.label}) — ${why}`).join("; ") + "." : "",
  ].filter(Boolean).join(" ");
}

/** The chapter-level reading rules: which movements are adverse, and which measures rest on too few records. */
export function readingGuide(ids: string[], n: number): string {
  const known = ids.filter(id => definition(id));
  const adverse = known.filter(id => definition(id)!.higherIsBetter === false);
  const thin = known.filter(id => n < definition(id)!.minSample);
  return [
    adverse.length ? `Lower is better, so a rise is adverse: ${adverse.map(id => `${id} (${definition(id)!.label})`).join(", ")}. Every other measure here improves when it rises. Never call an adverse rise an improvement.` : "",
    thin.length ? `Contributing records (${n}) are below the minimum sample for: ${thin.join(", ")}. Report these as indicative and give them no more than low confidence.` : "",
  ].filter(Boolean).join("\n");
}

```

```typescript
import { unsupportedReportMetrics } from "./policy";
import { chapters, type ChapterSpec } from "./chapters";
import { metrics } from "../semantics/metrics";
import { metricTable } from "../semantics/catalogue";
import { renewalMeasures } from "../data/renewals";

/**
 * Every measure is reported in exactly one chapter per population, so a figure
 * never appears twice in a report. Chapters that read the same population
 * (Schedule, Instructors and Formats all read Sessions) would otherwise repeat
 * attendance, fill and yield in each. Chapters on different populations
 * (Sessions versus Recurring, Leads versus Website leads) legitimately show
 * similarly named measures, because the numbers are different.
 */
const HOME_FIRST = ["sessions"];
const NEVER_OWN = new Set(["executive-summary", "recommendations", "predictions"]);

/** Chapters reading the same rows share a key. */
export const populationKey = (spec: ChapterSpec) =>
  `${spec.renewal ? "renewal" : spec.source}${spec.website ? "+website" : ""}${spec.network ? "+network" : ""}`;

/** The registry table a chapter's app tab reads; recurring chapters reuse the Sessions measures on lifetime facts. */
const tabSource = (spec: ChapterSpec) => (spec.source === "recurring" ? "sessions" : spec.source);

/** Everything the app tab's month-on-month table lists for this chapter's source. */
export function tabMetricIds(spec: ChapterSpec): string[] {
  if (spec.derived || NEVER_OWN.has(spec.id)) return [];
  if (spec.renewal) return Object.keys(renewalMeasures);
  const source = tabSource(spec);
  return Object.keys(metrics).filter(id => id !== "records" && !(spec.source === "recurring" && id === "draw_premium_pp") && metricTable(id) === source
    && (spec.website ? id.startsWith("website_") : !id.startsWith("website_")));
}

const explicit = (spec: ChapterSpec) => [...new Set([...spec.metrics, ...spec.history, ...spec.groups.flatMap(g => g.columns)])];

/** The chapter that is the home of a population: the one that reports its complete tab. */
export function homeChapter(spec: ChapterSpec): ChapterSpec {
  const same = chapters.filter(c => !NEVER_OWN.has(c.id) && !c.derived && populationKey(c) === populationKey(spec));
  return [...same].sort((a, b) => {
    const rank = (c: ChapterSpec) => HOME_FIRST.includes(c.id) ? 0 : 1;
    return rank(a) - rank(b);
  })[0] ?? spec;
}

/**
 * The measures this chapter reports in its register, month-on-month table and
 * metric cards. A home chapter reports its whole app tab; a sibling reports
 * only what the home does not.
 */
export function ownedMetricIds(spec: ChapterSpec): string[] {
  if (spec.derived || NEVER_OWN.has(spec.id)) return [];
  const home = homeChapter(spec);
  const homeSet = new Set([...tabMetricIds(home), ...explicit(home)]);
  const mine = home.id === spec.id ? [...tabMetricIds(spec), ...explicit(spec)] : explicit(spec).filter(id => !homeSet.has(id));
  return [...new Set(mine)].filter(id=>!unsupportedReportMetrics.has(id));
}

/** True when another chapter of the same population reports this measure. */
export const reportedElsewhere = (spec: ChapterSpec, id: string) => !spec.derived && !NEVER_OWN.has(spec.id) && !ownedMetricIds(spec).includes(id);

/** Where a measure is reported, for the pointer a sibling chapter shows. */
export function ownerOf(spec: ChapterSpec, id: string): ChapterSpec | undefined {
  const home = homeChapter(spec);
  return home.id !== spec.id && ownedMetricIds(home).includes(id) ? home : undefined;
}

```

```typescript
import type { ChapterData, GroupTable } from './model';
import { monthLabel, shiftMonth } from './period';

export interface EvidenceMatrix {
  metric: string;
  categories: string[];
  months?: string[];
  periods: { month?: string; label: string; values: (number | null)[] }[];
  shown: number;
  available: number;
  basis: string;
}
const measured = (value: unknown): number | null => value == null || value === '' || !Number.isFinite(Number(value)) ? null : Number(value);

/** One metric and a common scale. Missing cells are never converted to zero. */
export function groupMatrix(table: GroupTable, metric: string, month: string, highlights: string[] = [], limit = 8): EvidenceMatrix {
  const rows = table.rows.filter(row => [row[metric], table.prior?.[String(row.g)]?.[metric], table.priorYear?.[String(row.g)]?.[metric]].some(v => measured(v) != null));
  const selected = [...rows.filter(row => highlights.includes(String(row.g))), ...rows.filter(row => !highlights.includes(String(row.g)))].slice(0, limit);
  const periods = [
    { month: shiftMonth(month, -12), label: monthLabel(shiftMonth(month, -12)), values: selected.map(row => measured(table.priorYear?.[String(row.g)]?.[metric])) },
    { month: shiftMonth(month, -1), label: monthLabel(shiftMonth(month, -1)), values: selected.map(row => measured(table.prior?.[String(row.g)]?.[metric])) },
    { month, label: monthLabel(month), values: selected.map(row => measured(row[metric])) },
  ].filter(period => period.values.some(v => v != null));
  return { metric, categories: selected.map(row => String(row.g ?? 'Unspecified')), periods, shown: selected.length, available: rows.length,
    basis: `${selected.length} of ${rows.length} stored groups shown${table.omitted ? `; ${table.omitted} further eligible groups omitted from the saved ranking` : ''}. ${table.minimum}. Periods without observations are omitted; missing cells remain unavailable.` };
}
export function historyMatrix(data: ChapterData, metric: string, limit = 12): EvidenceMatrix {
  const rows = data.history.slice(-limit);
  return { metric, months: rows.map(row => String(row.month)), categories: rows.map(row => monthLabel(String(row.month))), periods: [{ label: 'Monthly observation', values: rows.map(row => measured(row[metric])) }], shown: rows.length, available: data.history.length,
    basis: `${rows.length} observed calendar months from the frozen report. Gaps are unavailable; values are not interpolated.` };
}
export function matrixDomain(matrix: EvidenceMatrix) {
  const values = matrix.periods.flatMap(p => p.values).filter((v): v is number => v != null && Number.isFinite(v));
  return { min: Math.min(0, ...values), max: Math.max(0, ...values), count: values.length };
}
```

```typescript
/** Creation verbs alone are not authorization to save an analytical element. */
export function agentIntent(message: string, selected: "ask" | "build" = "ask"): "ask" | "build" {
  if (/\b(?:do not|don't|dont|without|never)\s+(?:create|build|generate|make|add|save|plot|draw)\b/i.test(message)) return "ask";
  if (/^\s*(?:how\s+(?:do|can|would|should)\s+(?:i|we|you)|explain\s+how|what\s+is)\b/i.test(message)) return "ask";
  const creates = /\b(create|build|generate|make|add|save|plot|draw)\b/i.test(message);
  const artifact = /\b(charts?|tables?|graphs?|elements?|views?|insights?|lists?|dashboards?|pivots?|heat\s?maps?|kpis?|scorecards?|scatter|donuts?|combo)\b/i.test(message);
  return creates && artifact ? "build" : selected;
}
```

```typescript
import type { Row } from "../data/duckdb";
export function slotVerdict(row: Row, rate: number) {
  if (Number(row.n) < 8) return "Low sample";
  if (row.fill_rate == null || row.revenue_per_session == null)
    return "Unavailable";
  if (Number(row.fill_rate) < 0.2) return "Cut";
  if (Number(row.revenue_per_session) < rate) return "Move";
  return Number(row.fill_rate) < 0.4 ? "Watch" : "Keep";
}
export function revenueBridge(current: Row, previous: Row) {
  if (
    current.revenue == null ||
    previous.revenue == null ||
    !Number(previous.attendance)
  )
    return [];
  const before = Number(previous.revenue),
    after = Number(current.revenue),
    a0 = Number(previous.attendance),
    a1 = Number(current.attendance),
    yield0 = before / a0,
    yield1 = a1 ? after / a1 : 0;
  return [
    { name: "Prior period", value: before },
    { name: "Attendance volume", value: (a1 - a0) * yield0 },
    { name: "Realised yield", value: a1 * (yield1 - yield0) },
    { name: "Current period", value: after },
  ];
}
```

```typescript
import { metrics } from "./metrics";
import { sheets } from "../data/sheets.config";

/**
 * Which table a metric is computed over. A metric names its source columns as
 * "Sheet Title.Column"; several metrics read two sheets (payroll cost against
 * earned revenue, say) and are computed over the first, which is the one the
 * analytics layer joins the rest onto.
 */
export function metricTable(id: string): string | null {
  const titles = new Map(sheets.map((s) => [s.title.toLowerCase(), s.key]));
  for (const source of metrics[id]?.sources || []) {
    const title = source.split(".")[0].split(" → ")[0].trim().toLowerCase();
    const key = titles.get(title);
    if (key) return key;
  }
  return null;
}

export const domains = ["attendance", "revenue", "growth", "people", "risk"] as const;
export const domainLabels: Record<(typeof domains)[number], string> = {
  attendance: "Attendance & capacity",
  revenue: "Revenue & yield",
  growth: "Acquisition & growth",
  people: "Members & people",
  risk: "Risk & attrition",
};

export interface CatalogueEntry {
  id: string;
  table: string;
  domain: string;
}

/**
 * Every registered metric that can actually be computed, grouped by the table
 * it reads. `records` is excluded: it counts rows rather than measuring them.
 */
export function catalogue(): Map<string, CatalogueEntry[]> {
  const byTable = new Map<string, CatalogueEntry[]>();
  for (const id of Object.keys(metrics)) {
    if (id === "records") continue;
    const table = metricTable(id);
    if (!table) continue;
    const list = byTable.get(table) || [];
    list.push({ id, table, domain: metrics[id].domain });
    byTable.set(table, list);
  }
  return byTable;
}

```

```typescript
import { metrics } from "./metrics";
import { fmt, delta } from "./formats";

/**
 * Counts are exact at any sample size; only values derived from a sample —
 * rates, averages, medians — mislead when the sample is small.
 */
export function derived(id: string) {
  const m = metrics[id];
  return (
    ["percent", "ratio", "decimal", "days"].includes(m.format) ||
    ["weighted", "median", "avg"].includes(m.aggregation)
  );
}

/** Movement against the comparison period, using the shared delta wording. */
export function cellDelta(id: string, value: unknown, before: unknown) {
  if (value == null || before == null) return null;
  const now = Number(value),
    was = Number(before);
  if (!Number.isFinite(now) || !Number.isFinite(was)) return null;
  const text = delta(id, value, before);
  if (text === "No comparison" || text === "No baseline") return null;
  const change = now - was;
  return {
    text,
    tone:
      Math.abs(change) < Number.EPSILON
        ? "muted"
        : change > 0 === metrics[id].higherIsBetter
          ? "positive"
          : "negative",
  };
}

/** Everything behind the number, for the cell's tooltip. */
export function provenance(
  id: string,
  value: unknown,
  n: number,
  thin: boolean,
  before: unknown,
) {
  const m = metrics[id];
  const lines = [
    `${m.label}: ${fmt(id, value, true)}`,
    `Formula: ${m.description}`,
    `Source columns: ${m.sources.join(", ")}`,
    `Contributing records: ${fmt("records", n)}`,
  ];
  if (before != null)
    lines.push(`Comparison period: ${fmt(id, before, true)}`);
  if (thin)
    lines.push(
      `* Fewer than ${m.minSample} records. This is a derived value on a small sample — read it as a hint, not a result.`,
    );
  lines.push("Click to inspect the records behind this cell.");
  return lines.join("\n");
}

```

```typescript
/**
 * The saved-element contract shared by the agent (which writes it), the server (which
 * validates it against the real query result) and the workspace (which renders it).
 */
export const elementTypes = [
  "table",
  "list",
  "bar",
  "horizontal_bar",
  "stacked_bar",
  "line",
  "area",
  "combo",
  "pie",
  "donut",
  "scatter",
  "heatmap",
  "pivot",
  "kpi",
] as const;
export type ElementType = (typeof elementTypes)[number];
export const chartTypes: ElementType[] = ["bar", "horizontal_bar", "stacked_bar", "line", "area", "combo", "pie", "donut", "scatter", "heatmap"];

export interface ElementSpec {
  type: ElementType;
  sql: string;
  x: string;
  series: string[];
  y2: string[];
  group: string;
  value: string;
  compare: (string | null)[];
  /** Shows full history whatever the page's date filter; studio and other filters still apply. */
  ignoreDates: boolean;
}

const names = (v: unknown) => (Array.isArray(v) ? v.filter((s): s is string => typeof s === "string" && !!s) : typeof v === "string" && v ? [v] : []);
const name = (v: unknown) => (typeof v === "string" ? v : "");

/** Reads a stored body, including the original single-measure `{type,sql,x,y}` shape. */
export function elementSpec(body: any): ElementSpec {
  const series = names(body?.series);
  return {
    type: body?.type,
    sql: name(body?.sql),
    x: name(body?.x),
    series: series.length ? series : names(body?.y),
    y2: names(body?.y2),
    group: name(body?.group),
    value: name(body?.value),
    compare: Array.isArray(body?.compare) ? body.compare.map((c: unknown) => (typeof c === "string" && c ? c : null)) : [],
    ignoreDates: body?.ignoreDates === true,
  };
}

/** Field names, the reason the type needs them, and how many measures it takes. */
function requirements(s: ElementSpec): string | null {
  const need = (field: string, why: string) => `${s.type} needs "${field}" (${why}).`;
  switch (s.type) {
    case "bar":
    case "horizontal_bar":
    case "stacked_bar":
    case "line":
    case "area":
      if (!s.x) return need("x", "the category or time column");
      if (!s.series.length || s.series.length > 6) return `${s.type} needs "series" with 1–6 numeric columns.`;
      return null;
    case "combo":
      if (!s.x) return need("x", "the category or time column");
      if (!s.series.length) return need("series", "numeric columns drawn as bars on the left axis");
      if (!s.y2.length) return need("y2", "numeric columns drawn as lines on the right axis");
      if (s.series.length + s.y2.length > 6) return "combo takes at most 6 measures across series and y2.";
      return null;
    case "pie":
    case "donut":
    case "scatter":
      if (!s.x) return need("x", s.type === "scatter" ? "the numeric horizontal column" : "the slice label column");
      if (s.series.length !== 1) return `${s.type} needs exactly one column in "series".`;
      return null;
    case "heatmap":
    case "pivot":
      if (!s.x) return need("x", "the row dimension");
      if (!s.group) return need("group", "the column dimension");
      if (!s.value) return need("value", "the numeric cell value");
      return null;
    case "kpi":
      if (!s.series.length || s.series.length > 6) return 'kpi needs "series" with 1–6 numeric columns from a one-row result.';
      if (s.compare.length && s.compare.length !== s.series.length)
        return '"compare" must list one previous-period column (or null) for each series column, in the same order.';
      return null;
    default:
      return null;
  }
}

/**
 * Null when the body is a complete element. With `columns` (from running its SQL), also
 * proves every referenced field is a column of the result.
 */
export function elementSpecError(body: any, columns?: string[]): string | null {
  if (!elementTypes.includes(body?.type))
    return `Unsupported element type "${body?.type}". Use one of: ${elementTypes.join(", ")}.`;
  const s = elementSpec(body);
  if (!s.sql.trim()) return "An element needs its live \"sql\".";
  const missing = requirements(s);
  if (missing) return missing;
  if (columns?.length) {
    const fields = [s.x, ...s.series, ...s.y2, s.group, s.value, ...s.compare].filter((f): f is string => !!f);
    const absent = fields.find((f) => !columns.includes(f));
    if (absent)
      return `"${absent}" is not a column of the query result. Result columns: ${columns.join(", ")}. Alias the SQL columns or change the element fields to match.`;
  }
  return null;
}

/** Validate the result itself, not just the shape of the model's configuration. */
export function elementResultError(body: any, rows: Record<string, unknown>[], columns?: string[]): string | null {
  const invalid = elementSpecError(body, columns || Object.keys(rows[0] || {}));
  if (invalid) return invalid;
  if (!rows.length) return "The element query returned no rows. Check source coverage and scope before saving an empty element.";
  const s = elementSpec(body);
  if (s.type === "kpi" && rows.length !== 1) return "KPI cards require exactly one aggregated row. Aggregate the requested scope before saving.";
  const measures = [...s.series, ...s.y2, s.value, ...s.compare].filter((v): v is string => !!v);
  if (s.type === "scatter") measures.push(s.x);
  for (const field of new Set(measures)) {
    const values = rows.map(r => r[field]).filter(v => v != null && v !== "");
    if (!values.length) return `"${field}" has no measured values. Missing evidence cannot be plotted as zero.`;
    if (values.some(v => typeof v === "boolean" || !["number", "string"].includes(typeof v) || !Number.isFinite(Number(v))))
      return `"${field}" must contain numeric values; fix the query or select a numeric measure.`;
  }
  for (const field of [s.x, s.group].filter(Boolean))
    if (rows.every(r => r[field] == null || r[field] === "")) return `"${field}" has no populated categories. Choose a populated grouping field.`;
  if (["pie", "donut"].includes(s.type)) {
    if (rows.length > 8) return "Pie and donut charts support at most 8 slices. Group small categories into Other or use a bar chart.";
    if (rows.some(r => r[s.series[0]] != null && Number(r[s.series[0]]) < 0)) return "Pie and donut charts cannot show negative values. Use a bar chart.";
    if (!rows.some(r => Number(r[s.series[0]]) > 0)) return "Pie and donut charts require a positive measured total.";
  }
  if (["pivot", "heatmap"].includes(s.type)) {
    const seen = new Set<string>();
    for (const row of rows) {
      const key = JSON.stringify([row[s.x], row[s.group]]);
      if (seen.has(key)) return "The result contains multiple rows per matrix cell. Aggregate to one row per dimension pair using the governed metric definition.";
      seen.add(key);
    }
  }
  return null;
}

/** Rates, averages and shares do not add up across cells, so they get no totals. */
const nonAdditive = /(rate|pct|percent|avg|average|mean|median|per_|ratio|share|fill|aov|ltv|_size|yield)/i;

export function pivotRows(rows: Record<string, unknown>[], x: string, group: string, value: string) {
  const rowKeys: string[] = [];
  const colKeys: string[] = [];
  const cells = new Map<string, number>();
  const key = (r: string, c: string) => r + "\u0000" + c;
  for (const row of rows) {
    const r = String(row[x] ?? "—"),
      c = String(row[group] ?? "—");
    if (!rowKeys.includes(r)) rowKeys.push(r);
    if (!colKeys.includes(c)) colKeys.push(c);
    const v = row[value];
    if (v != null && v !== "" && Number.isFinite(Number(v))) cells.set(key(r, c), (cells.get(key(r, c)) ?? 0) + Number(v));
  }
  // Months, dates and times read left to right; named columns (weekdays, studios) keep query order.
  if (colKeys.every((c) => /^\d/.test(c))) colKeys.sort((a, b) => a.localeCompare(b, undefined, { numeric: true }));
  const cell = (r: string, c: string) => cells.get(key(r, c)) ?? null;
  const sum = (values: (number | null)[]) => values.reduce<number>((t, v) => t + (v ?? 0), 0);
  return {
    rowKeys,
    colKeys,
    cell,
    totals: !nonAdditive.test(value),
    rowTotal: (r: string) => sum(colKeys.map((c) => cell(r, c))),
    colTotal: (c: string) => sum(rowKeys.map((r) => cell(r, c))),
    total: sum([...cells.values()]),
  };
}

/** Element forms a request names explicitly, or null when it leaves the form open. */
const namedForms: [RegExp, ElementType[]][] = [
  [/\b(tables?|tabular|spreadsheet)\b/i, ["table", "pivot", "list"]],
  [/\b(pivot|matrix|cross-?tab)\b/i, ["pivot"]],
  [/\bheat ?maps?\b/i, ["heatmap"]],
  [/\b(kpis?|scorecards?|cards?|tiles?)\b/i, ["kpi"]],
  [/\blists?\b/i, ["list", "table"]],
  [/\b(line|area) (charts?|graphs?)\b/i, ["line", "area"]],
  [/\b(bar|column) (charts?|graphs?)\b|\bbars?\b/i, ["bar", "horizontal_bar", "stacked_bar"]],
  [/\bstacked\b/i, ["stacked_bar"]],
  [/\b(pie|donut|doughnut)\b/i, ["pie", "donut"]],
  [/\bscatter\b/i, ["scatter"]],
  [/\bcombo\b|\bdual[- ]axis\b/i, ["combo"]],
];
export function requestedElementTypes(message: string): ElementType[] | null {
  const types = new Set<ElementType>();
  for (const [pattern, forms] of namedForms) if (pattern.test(message)) forms.forEach((t) => types.add(t));
  return types.size ? [...types] : null;
}

/** Requests whose element must span months beyond whatever period the page is showing. */
export function wantsFullHistory(message: string): boolean {
  return /\b(mom|m-o-m|month[- ]on[- ]month|month[- ]over[- ]month|month[- ]by[- ]month|monthly trend|yoy|year[- ]on[- ]year|year[- ]over[- ]year|all[- ]time|full history|every month)\b/i.test(message)
    || /\b(not|never|n't)\b[^.]{0,30}\b(affected|filtered|changed|limited)\b[^.]{0,20}\b(date|period)/i.test(message)
    || /\b(ignore|regardless of|independent of|irrespective of)\b[^.]{0,20}\b(date|period)/i.test(message);
}
```

```typescript
import { metrics } from "./metrics";
export function fmt(id: string, v: unknown, full = false): string {
  if (v == null || !Number.isFinite(Number(v))) return "—";
  const n = Number(v);
  if (id === "draw_premium_pp")
    return `${n >= 0 ? "+" : ""}${(n * 100).toFixed(1)}pp`;
  switch (metrics[id]?.format) {
    case "currency":
      return !full && Math.abs(n) >= 1e7
        ? `₹${(n / 1e7).toFixed(1)}Cr`
        : !full && Math.abs(n) >= 1e5
          ? `₹${(n / 1e5).toFixed(1)}L`
          : // Whole rupees when written in full; decimals only accompany L / Cr.
            new Intl.NumberFormat("en-IN", {
              style: "currency",
              currency: "INR",
              maximumFractionDigits: 0,
            }).format(n);
    case "percent":
      return `${(n * 100).toFixed(1)}%`;
    case "ratio":
      return `${n.toFixed(1)}×`;
    case "days":
      return `${n.toFixed(1)}d`;
    case "decimal":
      return n.toFixed(1);
    default:
      return new Intl.NumberFormat("en-IN", {
        maximumFractionDigits: 0,
      }).format(n);
  }
}
export function delta(id: string, current: unknown, previous: unknown): string {
  if (current == null || previous == null) return "No comparison";
  const c = Number(current),
    p = Number(previous);
  if (metrics[id]?.format === "percent") {
    const d = (c - p) * 100;
    return `${d >= 0 ? "+" : ""}${d.toFixed(1)}pp`;
  }
  if (!p) return "No baseline";
  const d = (c / p - 1) * 100;
  return `${d >= 0 ? "+" : ""}${d.toFixed(1)}%`;
}

/** Display source and generated fields without rounding identifiers or changing exported data. */
export function formatField(field: string, value: unknown): string {
  if (value == null) return "—";
  if (typeof value === "boolean") return value ? "Yes" : "No";
  if (metrics[field]) return fmt(field, value, true);
  if (/\b(id|phone|email|token|reference|code)\b/i.test(field.replaceAll("_", " ")) || /(?:^|_)(?:date|month|time|snapshot)(?:_|$)|\b(?:date|month|time|snapshot)\b/i.test(field)) return String(value);
  const text = String(value).trim();
  if (!/^-?(?:₹\s*)?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?$/.test(text)) return text;
  const number = Number(text.replace(/[₹,\s]/g, ""));
  if (!Number.isFinite(number)) return text;
  const isCount = /count|known|missing|rows|lines|records|quantity|credits|rank/i.test(field);
  if (!isCount && /revenue|spend|amount|price|cost|paid|payment value|vat|discount|gross.sales|net.sales|total.sales|sales.total|(?:total|left|paid|balance).*money|money.*(?:left|total|balance)/i.test(field.replaceAll("_", " "))) return fmt("revenue", number, true);
  return new Intl.NumberFormat("en-IN", {maximumFractionDigits:1}).format(number);
}
```

### src/semantics/membership-eligibility.ts

Symbols: sqlString, name, paidMembershipSQL, LAPSE_GRACE_DAYS, recordedStatus, confirmedLapseSQL, latestLapseSQL

SQL output aliases: a, lapsed, DATE, rank

```typescript
import { today } from "../data/periods";
import { EXCLUDED_MEMBERSHIP_PATTERNS, EXCLUDED_MEMBERSHIP_TERMS } from "../../server/kra-churn.mjs";

const sqlString = (s: string) => `'${s.replaceAll("'", "''")}'`;
const name = "lower(COALESCE(product,''))";

/**
 * A paid membership whose name is not on the business's restricted list — the same
 * rules the KRA churn measure uses (server/kra-churn.mjs). Frozen is handled by callers:
 * a frozen membership still counts as a member's latest membership, but never as lapsed.
 */
export const paidMembershipSQL = [
  "COALESCE(amount_paid,0)>0",
  ...EXCLUDED_MEMBERSHIP_TERMS.map((term) => `NOT contains(${name},${sqlString(term)})`),
  ...EXCLUDED_MEMBERSHIP_PATTERNS.map((pattern) => `NOT regexp_matches(${name},${sqlString(pattern.source)})`),
].join(" AND ");

/** Days after the Churned Date before a Lapsed membership counts as lapsed; until then it is in grace. */
export const LAPSE_GRACE_DAYS = 30;
const recordedStatus = (alias = "") => `lower(trim(COALESCE(${alias}status,'')))`;
/** Status is Lapsed and the Churned Date (End Date when blank) is at least 30 days before the as-of date. */
export const confirmedLapseSQL = (asOf: string, alias = "") =>
  `${recordedStatus(alias)}='lapsed' AND TRY_CAST(COALESCE(${alias}churned_date,${alias}end_date) AS DATE)<=DATE '${asOf}'-INTERVAL ${LAPSE_GRACE_DAYS} DAY`;

/**
 * Flags each member's most recent paid, unrestricted membership when its recorded Status is
 * Lapsed at least 30 days past the Churned Date (so Frozen, Not Activated, Active, New, Renewed
 * and still-in-grace memberships are not lapses). Lapsed members count only these rows, so a
 * member who later bought another paid membership is not counted as lapsed.
 * Depends on the as-of date: re-run whenever the table loads or is restored.
 */
export const latestLapseSQL = (table = "lapsed", asOf = today()) => `UPDATE "${table}" SET latest_lapse = (r.rank = 1 AND ${confirmedLapseSQL(asOf, `"${table}".`)})
FROM (SELECT row_id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY member_id ORDER BY TRY_CAST(start_date AS DATE) DESC NULLS LAST, TRY_CAST(end_date AS DATE) DESC NULLS LAST, row_id DESC) AS rank
  FROM "${table}" WHERE member_id IS NOT NULL AND ${paidMembershipSQL}) r
WHERE "${table}".row_id = r.row_id`;
```

### src/semantics/metrics.ts

SQL output aliases: MetricDef

```typescript
import { evidenceSQL } from "./evidence";
import registry from "./registry.json";
export interface QueryContext {
  rate: number;
  today: string;
  newWhere?: string;
}
export interface MetricDef {
  id: string;
  label: string;
  description: string;
  domain: "attendance" | "revenue" | "growth" | "people" | "risk";
  format: "currency" | "percent" | "integer" | "decimal" | "ratio" | "days";
  sql: (ctx: QueryContext) => string;
  aggregation: "sum" | "weighted" | "median" | "avg" | "last";
  higherIsBetter: boolean;
  target?: number;
  minSample: number;
  sources: string[];
}
export const metrics: Record<string, MetricDef> = Object.fromEntries(
  registry.map((m) => [
    m.id,
    {
      ...m,
      description: m.expression,
      sql: (ctx: QueryContext) =>
        m.expression
          .replace("(SELECT AVG(first_purchase) FROM new WHERE is_new)", `(SELECT AVG(first_purchase) FROM new${ctx.newWhere || " WHERE TRUE"} AND is_new AND conversion='Converted' AND first_purchase>0)`)
          .replaceAll("{rate}", String(ctx.rate))
          .replaceAll("{today}", ctx.today),
    } as MetricDef,
  ]),
);
export const metricSQL = (ids: string[], ctx: QueryContext) =>
  ids.map((id) => `${metrics[id].sql(ctx)} AS "${id}"${evidenceSQL(id)}`).join(", ");

// The records behind a single cell: a metric's first FILTER (WHERE …) clause is
// its numerator condition, so a drill-down can show only the contributing rows.
export function contributorPredicate(id: string, ctx: QueryContext) {
  const expression = metrics[id]?.sql(ctx);
  if (!expression) return undefined;
  const start = expression.indexOf("FILTER (WHERE ");
  if (start < 0) return undefined;
  let depth = 1;
  let i = start + "FILTER (".length;
  const from = i + "WHERE ".length;
  for (i = from; i < expression.length && depth > 0; i++) {
    if (expression[i] === "(") depth++;
    else if (expression[i] === ")") depth--;
  }
  return depth === 0 ? expression.slice(from, i - 1).trim() : undefined;
}

/** The protected rate denominator, when the registry explicitly supplies one. */
export function metricDenominatorSQL(id:string,ctx:QueryContext):string|null {
  const expression=metrics[id]?.sql(ctx);if(!expression)return null;
  if(metrics[id].aggregation==='avg'||metrics[id].aggregation==='median') {const match=/^(?:AVG|MEDIAN)\(([^()]+)\)/i.exec(expression.trim());return match?expression.trim().replace(/^(AVG|MEDIAN)/i,'COUNT'):null;}
  if(metrics[id].aggregation!=='weighted')return null;
  const start=expression.indexOf('NULLIF(');if(start<0)return null;
  let depth=0;for(let i=start+7;i<expression.length;i++){if(expression[i]==='(')depth++;else if(expression[i]===')')depth--;else if(expression[i]===','&&depth===0)return expression.slice(start+7,i).trim();}
  return null;
}
```
